items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: Sonny Boy asked my mother if I could join his group, which was working at the barbecue stand on 3rd Avenue and 14th Street

ctx.x: So I played, between the UNIA Marching Band and St. Agnes Marching Band, I played with these two until I reached the age of around 12½.

And I'll never forget, I played my first gig -- it was on the fourth of July, at the UNIA Hall in 1931, and I wasn't 13 yet -- I wasn't 13 until that December. And I did so well, until I was asked by a fellow around Miami, a saxophone player named Sonny Boy, and Sonny Boy asked my mother if I could join his group, which was working at the barbecue stand on 3rd Avenue and 14th Street -- it was sort of a juke joint, and we used to play there five nights a week, and each night, there was either a good shooting scrap…
This was where I formed that fondness for upright pianos, because many a night when they got to shooting, that was where the whole band could be found -- behind the piano.
